item.title: Michael Porter Jr. Again Stands Athwart History, Saying “Damn, That’s Crazy”
item.author: Patrick Redford
item.content:encoded: It is late August, the waning days of a long summer. Though the oppressive heat still imposes itself on you, the days are shortening noticeably, the faint whisper of a chill in the air perceptible in the stiller moments of deep night. Soon there will be red leaves, sweaters onto shoulders, and NBA basketball.You both anticipate and fear the turnover of the seasons, though it feels abstract—that is, until your phone lights up. Someone has sent you an Instagram link to a clip from Michael Porter Jr.'s podcast, , where he and Lonzo Ball are inadvertently inventing effective altruism from first principles. Unable to look away, you scroll further and select a clip with the banner text "HOW WOMEN ARE TOXIC," and the captioned text "girls be toxic," learning about how these females often display toxic tendencies. , you think to yourself, Brooklyn Nets basketball is right around the corner.Porter Jr. is a figure of fascination around these parts, as he is a starting-caliber NBA player who is seemingly more dedicated to cutting odious podcast clips than he is to helping his team win basketball games. Last offseason, Porter Jr. called attention to himself—it wouldn't be quite right to say he "got himself in trouble" or "generated controversy," since those formulations presuppose both a consensus reality against which he clashed, and a mechanism of consequence that doesn't exist—by going on one of the Nelk Boys' podcasts and saying stuff like, "I'm not saying I'm a misogynist or anything, but I'll throw on some Andrew Tate and see how they react," because you have to "test a girl early" and "do your research." It was an occasion to reflect on the alarming, shrinking distance between high-level athletes and the internecine culture of the right-wing internet, which is to say: the internet.

item.title: What Makes A Good Critic?
item.author: Drew Magary
item.content:encoded: Drew Magary’s Thursday Afternoon NFL Dick Joke Jamboroo runs every Thursday at Defector during the NFL season. Got something you wanna contribute? . You can also read Drew over at“Everyone’s a critic” has been a lament my entire life, but the advent of the internet rendered it literally true. Anyone can review anything online, from new albums to tubes of toothpaste. But just because you can review something doesn’t mean you’re doing criticism. It’s easy to conflate the two nouns, especially now that the occupation of professional critic is all but extinct. Every critic out of a job has been replaced by an endless crowd of civilian reviewers, which means fewer enlightening pieces of cultural criticism. That sucks for a lot of reasons, but above all, it leaves the culture at large unable to understand what good criticism looks like, or even what criticism .Because criticism isn’t just me telling you “This was great” or “This sucked.” A good critic provides necessary context to whatever it is that they’re evaluating. My favorite music critic ever is Stephen Thomas Erlewine, who used to review albums for AllMusic before the site cut him loose and he was forced to open up his own Substack. Erlewine knows far, far more about music than I do. He's listened to every previous album/B-side an artist has put out before reviewing their newest release. He knows the background story of how that album was made. He knows if the lead singer and lead guitarist stopped talking to each other a week into the recording sessions. He knows the producer of the album, and he’s heard all of the other albums that producer has made. He’ll render a final judgment on a work, as the job requires, but he’s done enough homework to make certain that his is an judgment.

item.title: Trump DOJ Now Targeting Ballots, Not Just Voter Rolls
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: For transparency reasons, I like peeling back the curtain on any changes we make to Morning Memo — but doing so always runs the risk of creating some confusion. So let me be really clear upfront: The change I’m about to mention doesn’t require you to do anything differently on your end.Beginning next week, we’re going to be using a new email provider to send out Morning Memo each day. If you already receive Morning Memo by email, it will still come to you the same as usual, but it will come directly from TPM instead of from Substack. It might look a tad different in your inbox — and the email itself will look more like TPM — so I wanted you to be aware in advance.You’ll still be able to read Morning Memo in the email version or on Substack or at TPM. Your choice.We’re making this change because in this deeply fractured media world, we’re trying to build out the TPM ecosystem and not be overly reliant on outside platforms. Better to live and die on our own merits than be subject to the vagaries of third parties.OK, let’s get to today’s news.A Hugely Important DistinctionAs I feared, the developing story on the Trump DOJ targeting actual ballots in Los Angeles County is creating some confusion.I tried in yesterday’s Morning Memo to make clear that this was different in kind and degree from the Trump administration’s previous efforts to purge voter rolls in advance of the election. But the reactions I’ve seen since, both to what I wrote and in the larger coverage, suggest that’s still not coming across entirely clearly.Ironically, the Trump DOJ turns out to be helpful in this regard because it’s now admitted to NBC News that this is in fact different from a purge of voter rolls: “A DOJ spokesperson said the department is asking California to sequester ballots, not change their voter list.”Now, the Trump DOJ has its own reasons for making that distinction, among them trying to get around the federal statute that bars the mass purging of voter rolls in the 90 days before the election. But in this instance what the Trump DOJ is saying also happens to be true — and the truth is even more damning. Its election interference is no longer hypothetical; it’s happening now while real ballots are being cast.Once you make the category distinction between voter rolls and actual ballots already cast or soon to be cast, the seriousness of the threat from the federal government becomes a lot more obvious. The Trump DOJ is demanding that a specific batch of ballots be sequestered and not counted until citizenship is confirmed — an additional step in the tabulation process not provided for by law and which experts say would lead to a rushed and sloppy process that likely to disenfranchise legal voters.The threat is serious even if the Trump DOJ is unable to cite any lawful authority for its demand to California and even if there is no legal basis for it to order states to sequester ballots of people the Trump DOJ claims to have identified as “likely noncitizen voters.”With that framework in mind, let’s run through the latest developments and the big questions still outstanding …The Latest From California …: The Oct. 13 demand letter that acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter (the No. 2 official at DOJ!) sent to California Secretary ‌of State Shirley Weber. In a statement, Secretary ‌of State Weber revealed that the “password-protected thumb drive” containing the Trump DOJ’s list of “likely noncitizen voters” that McCotter references in his letters was accompanied by … wait for it … a sticky note with the password on it. Top notch information security going on there at the Trump DOJ.Say More About “Election Integrity”: Popping an unsecured thumb drive (see sticky note above) into a USB port in your election office is just not something election administrators not named Tina Peters would dream of doing. “We have not accessed the drive because doing so would conflict with established data privacy and information security protocols,” Logan, the Los Angeles County election official, said in a statement. “We do not consider the device a secure medium.” This is not the first time that the “election integrity” crowd has revealed how little regard it has for actual secure processes and procedures.JUST IN: Trump DOJ List Challenged in CourtThis morning, the UCLA Voting Rights Project, on behalf of the Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights and a Los Angeles resident, sought a temporary restraining order to preempt the Trump DOJ’s actions in California.The requested TRO, filed in an existing case in D.C. against Attorney General Todd Blanche and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, seeks to block the Trump DOJ from coercing California officials into using its purported list of “likely noncitizen voters” to withhold ballots from voters or to segregate and not count ballots already cast.U.S. District Judge Sparkle L. Sooknanan did not immediately scheduled a hearing on the TRO but set a deadline of 5 p.m. ET Friday for the parties to file a proposed briefing schedule.The big outstanding questions include:How many people are on the Trump DOJ list? Since McCotter doesn’t say in his letters and California officials haven’t even opened the file, we don’t know how long the Trump DOJ’s list of “likely noncitizen voters” actually is. A DOJ spokesperson allowed to the LA Times that the number is “in the thousands.” That’s a pretty big range.Did all or just some California counties receive a similar letter from the Trump DOJ? Similar letters were mailed out to other California counties, CBS News reports, but it’s not clear if it went to all or just some of them.Has the Trump DOJ targeted other states with similar demand letters? While the thrust of the Trump DOJ’s election-chaos has been aimed at blue states, there are tight House races in red states, too, where chaos might serve to delegitimize election results unfavorable to the GOP. Also worth noting that red state officials might be cooperative and not as quick to go public as California officials were.If you know of similar efforts by the Trump DOJ in other states, please get in touch with me via the encrypted methods here.‘Amateur Hour at the Department of Justice’UCLA election law expert Rick Hasen, in a not-so-succinct headline: “DOJ’s Threat Letter to California Voting Officials with a 48-Hour Deadline is Amateurish Political Theater Aimed at Sowing Chaos, Not to Mention a Demand That Likely Violates Federal Law and Election Security Practices”The Retribution: Ilhan Omar EditionThe one-two punch of retributive investigations of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN) by both the Department of Homeland Security and Department of Justice is looking worse the more that comes out:Denaturalization Is Trump’s Goal: The WSJ confirms that the investigation of Omar is “aimed at building a case to strip her of her U.S. citizenship and ultimately deport her.”: D.C. U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro, who touted her office’s role in the DOJ investigation of Omar during a Fox News appearance this week, was suspended by the same network in 2019, when she hosted a show there, for on-air comments about Omar: “Omar wears a hijab, which, according to the Quran 33:59, tells women to cover so they won’t get molested.” Pirro said at the time. “Is her adherence to this Islamic doctrine indicative of her adherence to Sharia law, which in itself is antithetical to the United States Constitution?”: U.S. Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh of D.C. did in fact limit the scope of the search warrant for Omar’s D.C. home after a protracted back and forth, CNN reports. In doing so, Sharbaugh reportedly cited precedent that preserves the protections for member of Congress contained in the Constitution’s Speech or Debate Clause. Nonetheless, Omar’s phone was among the items seized during the search of her home, NBC News reports.Trump: Execute the Leakers

item.title: Only One Michigan Senate Candidate Knows Puck
item.author: Lauren Theisen
item.content:encoded: There are two men running for Senate in Michigan, and one of them sucks. See if you can guess which one based on their official statements about the condition of the Detroit Red Wings, solicited by the blog Octopus Thrower. For context, the Red Wings hold the longest active playoff drought in the NHL by three seasons; don't currently employ an official, non-interim GM; haven't yet agreed to a new deal with young defensive standout Simon Edvinsson; can't seem to solve the problem of ex-captain Dylan Larkin's trade demand; and are dealing with dwindling fan interest as they've won just one of their first six games. Anyway, here's one candidate's statement:I was at the game when Darren McCarty took on Claude Lemieux. The ‘97 and ‘98 Stanley Cup championships are still highlights of my childhood. The teams the last few years have been a far cry from the Wings I came to love as a kid. They’re stacking losing season on losing season, yet the Ilitch family’s wealth has done nothing but grow. Michiganders are sick of sky-high ticket and concession prices buying them nothing but disappointment.The team holding out on Simon Edvinsson is just the latest example in a long series of ownership prioritizing their bottom line over the team and the fans. Our teams aren’t just assets for billionaires, they’re part of our culture and heritage. Hockeytown deserves better.

item.title: Where You Should Live: Five Factors to Keep in Mind
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: I ran across this post on Instagram by Bobby in Space (who posts about design and the psychology of place) and wanted to pull it onto the actual internet. Here are some snippets of his “5 hills I will die on as someone who studies the psychology of place”. I don’t think these are universal (e.g. people who live in rural areas likely prioritize other needs) or even necessarily the most important considerations (climate, sunlight, crime, schools), but they resonated with me.1. Your 10-minute radius matters more than almost anything else about where you live: Think about what you can get to in ten minutes without making it a whole thing. I can get coffee, get groceries, go to a park, and go to a friend’s place.This is the biggest thing that was missing for me living in rural VT for the past 10 years. My 10-minute radius required a car to access and even then was not teeming with options. My 10-minute radius here in Tokyo is, obviously, . It makes me so happy. A photo I took inside my 10-minute area a couple of weeks ago:2. More space can give you a smaller life: This one I’ll actually argue about. Idk why we’re obsessed with getting more sq footage, but sometimes the bigger house means you spend way more time inside it. House, car, work, car, house. Meanwhile, someone in a tiny apartment might walk downstairs, grab coffee, run into someone they know, walk to dinner, stop at the park. Technically they have less space. Butttttt their actual life might be way bigger.One of the things living in NYC taught me was how to treat the city as an extension of your home. I’m not sure people who live in rural and suburban areas think that way about the relationship between their homes and locations.3. The best neighborhood amenity might literally just be other people outside. […] You don’t even need to talk to any of them. Just seeing other people out living their lives makes you feel like you’re part of something.Yep. I have been so missing this in my life. My first few days here in Tokyo, I was craving being in huge crowds of humanity so much that I spent a lot of time in ultra-busy areas like Shinjuku and Shibuya.4. Moving somewhere new will change you, just probably not in the way you think: trust me, I still tend to do this. I think that a new city can solve all my problems. But it will not. You’re still going to be you.Haha, yeeeeep. Even a month into my travels, I have been disappointed to learn that my bad habits are still with me. Would really like to speak to the manager about that one…5. Where your friends live should influence where you live way more than we admit: I don’t even feel the need to explain this one. Relationships are the most important thing you’ll do in your life. Go live near people that light you upEven though it’s halfway across the world from where I’ve been living for the past 50+ years, I’ve seen more friends here in Japan in the past month than in the past 3 months in VT. It’s not going to be like that everywhere I go and I’m not near the most important folks in my life here, but it’s nice to have it while I’m here.

item.title: It’s Wheel of Moron Thursday: Ordinary tales of perfectly normal dumbfuckery
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: Yesterday was another one of those days where the stupid was so ungodly thick, you could cut it with a knife. Here a stupid, there a stupid, everywhere a stupid stupid — and you know what that means: it’s time once again to roll out the good old Big Wheel of Moron™, give it a vigorous spin, and see where it lands. Ready? .Oh look, here’s a perfectly normal thing that happens every day. It’s just United States President Rottinghands McCankles, being bundled into Helicopter Force One (or whatever the fuck it’s called), along with Diaper Nurse Natalie Harp and Found Object Katie Zacharia.Holy shit, look at the intensity with which these two women are focusing their rictus grins on the object of their affection.Who thought this was a wise idea? You can’t do this. You can’t take two fixated weirdos who both believe they have the god-ordained right to be the Fourth Mrs. Donny™ and put them in close quarters. It’s like shoving matter and antimatter together. Nothing good is going to happen. Bunnies are going to get boiled. Lots and lots of bunnies.If we could somehow take the barely-suppressed, seething resentment that these two rivals are developing for each other, and somehow hook it to a generator, it could be America’s greatest source of renewable energy.We’d better get out of here before we become collateral damage. Let’s give that Big Wheel of Moron™ another spin.“I love you too sir. In a totally platonic way, to be clear. I’m the vice president, not James Talarico.”GET IT? GET IT? JAMES TALARICO IS THE GAY! (Spoiler alert: he’s not.)I’m so tired of neanderthal assholes like JD Vance, whose homophobic sense of ‘humor’ — if we can charitably call it that — never matured beyond the eighth-grade locker room. It’s so fucking adolescent.This is what you do when your party is utterly devoid of accomplishments, and bereft of anything positive to run on — you just make up stupid shit about your opponent. Why does Couchfuck imagine that ‘’ is still a thing you can lob at someone? Bro, this is the year of our lord 2026. Open your eyes — no one cares. So what if Talarico the gayest gay in all of gaydom? We’ve over that shit. But beyond that, why is Couchfuck even being trotted out to campaign on behalf of loser candidates? He has zero charisma. He has no ability to connect with average people. He’s complete shit at small talk.‘So how’s your sexuality? Are you still straight? HA HA THAT’S GREAT!’Wheel of Moron™, kindly get us the fuck away from this repellent dipshit.“Mutilate your children, they want to mutilate, cut your children. It’s unbelievable, what they do. Six states, I mean they could do whatever the want, and they do. Your son leaves as Jimmy and comes home in three days as Janet, and they don’t even ask you. Most people don’t believe it. You know, they think it’s like an exaggeration. It’s not. They can take your child out of school and do whatever the hell they want. These people are sick. Minnesota is one of those states that can do that.”For fuck’s sake, Preznit Fuckwit has been vomiting out this fever-swamp hallucination for years now, and it doesn’t even stand up to ten seconds’ worth of critical thinking. Imagine that this were true. Imagine that you were the parent of darling little Jimmy, and one day he doesn’t get off the school bus. And then what? You just sit there for three days, going ‘well I guess he’s okay, wherever he is.’ Of course not.You know, Donny thinks he’s doing his party a favor, by showing up to ostensibly ‘campaign’ for a candidate, and then shitting nonsense like this out of his corroded face-hole instead. He’s not. Just like his furniture-fornicating Vice President, he’s become kryptonite to voters. Nobody but the brain-deadest of cultists want to hear Donny prattle on about Phelan said it’s doing nothing, because no one cares about the few dozen transgender people in sports. They just want cheap gas.Okay, that’s enough from our Moron-in-Chief. Let’s spin that Big Wheel again.“But remember, I’m the only one who took the test. You know, the aptitude test or whatever the hell they call it. I took it— when I did— every time I do a physical— I take a mental test. And I’ve aced it. WHERE’S MY DOCTOR? Is he around, I travel with more doctors than any human. If people get sick in the audience, they don’t— do— they leave him alone. You know what they call him? Collateral damage. If that person right over there, he looks like shit actually. He looks— he looks like he’s ready to have a heart attack. If he actually had a heart attack, you know what they would do? They would leave him alone.” The stupid shit thinks he’s been taking an ‘aptitude’ test. He’s not — it’s a test. And if you’re being asked to take one every time you have a checkup, it’s because your doctor has an excellent reason to suspect you have Don’t you love the way Donny boasts about acing his dementia test, and then careens wildly into the kind of incoherent anecdote that only a dementia sufferer would tell? Way to connect with your audience, you rotting dumbfuck. People can’t afford food. They can’t afford housing. They can’t afford basic goods and services. no one can afford healthcare — and this out-of-touch nincompoop is bragging about how he has all the doctors in the world, and you don’t. What in the actual fuck?Sigh. Let’s give that Big Wheel one final spin. Goddammit, it landed on Donny a third time. I’m going have to take this thing in and get it calibrated. The veeblefetzer is out of whack again. This is why, when they broadcast Dear Leader’s hate-rallies on TV, they’re always cropped in tightly from the front, on Donny and the worshipers who have been placed behind him — because if they showed you a wider view, you’d learn that no one is showing up to these things. The arena is nearly empty. He’s the crowd-size obsessed president, and he can’t draw a crowd. How sad is that? Wait, did I said it was sad? Actually, I meant to say that shit’s fucking hilarious.I swear, I’m trying really hard not to laugh.Now let’s move on to the one person on whom the Wheel of Moron would have never landed. That’s right, it’s time for our Daily Claudia.This first one, I have no clue where or when it was taken.This next one is from some poolside, , in 1992.And, lastly, check out these two weirdos, back in the early 1990s.Have a great Thursday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Anthropic tells investors quarterly revenue up nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of IPO
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: The phrase "told investors" appears four times in this FT article, which reports on Anthropic's day of hosting investors on Wednesday. Lots of details in here from "people with knowledge of the matter".Key things I learned from the article:Q1 revenue (Jan/Feb/Mar) was "about $4.8bn"Q2 (Apr/May/Jun) was $11.5bnQ3 (Jul/Aug/Sep) was $16.8bnIn Q3: $1.70 in revenue for every $1 spent on "computing power"Adjusted operating margins (excluding stock-based compensation) were 11%This point about distillation is worth quoting in full (highlight mine):The start-up has also clamped down on “distillation” — a controversial practice whereby rival AI labs train their models on the outputs of more advanced ones.When rival companies “distil” their models from Anthropic’s models, that involves heavy usage and spending.Anthropic told investors on Wednesday distillation accounted for 5 per cent to 7 per cent of revenue and that they had cut it back “materially” in the third quarter of the year, said four people with direct knowledge of the matter.Napkin maths says that if distillation was 5% of their Q2 revenue (before they cut it back in Q3) then unnamed "other labs" spent over half a billion dollars distilling Anthropic's models in that quarter!Also notable: Anthropic appear to no longer be leaning on "annualized run-rate revenue" (previously) in these communications to their investors.

item.title: Francis Fukuyama Is The Last Grandpa
item.author: Mathias Fuelling
item.content:encoded: If you’re not following Francis Fukuyama on Instagram, you’re missing out. His posts exemplify a Boomer picaresque aesthetic: the occasional typo in his captions, pictures of electronic parts that he’s fiddling with, a linear algebra textbook, a landscape shot of the Danube, mysterious but alluring architectural highlights of various European cities, and unsmiling selfies while wearing a ballcap. It’s all charming, yet interspersed within the grid are more eyebrow-raising indications: a debate with Peter Thiel at the Aspen Ideas Festival; pictures of meetings with various political figures, including a former PM of Turkey and Alexei Navalny; highlights of conferences and summits featuring a program he runs at Stanford University, the Leadership Academy for Development; and giving a talk to an organization called the Chicago Council on Global Affairs. How did he get here? Fukuyama’s memoir In the Realm of the Last Man offers a kind of answer, though perhaps not in the way that he intended. The title of Fukuyama’s memoir references the 1992 book that made his reputation. Long after Fukuyama is dead, and the rest of his work is gathering dust in libraries, The End of History and the Last Man will remain a point of reference. The book was an expansion of an earlier 1989 article he wrote as a first attempt to historicize the meaning of the end of the Cold War. Fukuyama in the book took a particular interpretation of Hegel as propounded by the Russian-French philosopher and civil servant Alexandre Kojève. Given Marx’s line that he stood Hegel right side up, Fukuyama can be said to have turned Hegel sideways: History has a kind of structural developmental logic to it, as determined by the human drive for recognition and respect, encapsulated by the Greek term . Iterations of the demand for have created conflict and change throughout history, determining the form of the state through time. For Fukuyama, the liberal capitalist order that won the Cold War, as led by the U.S., was the end of history, in that there would be no further political developments toward new kinds of state orders. This is not a triumphant vision, however, as at the end of the book he theorized the Last Man, a product of this world capitalist order, whose needs would be easily met and who would have no desire to strive for achievement or greatness, as his would be so easily assuaged. This Last Man would be a pathetic figure, a mere passive consumer and the society that created him would stagnate culturally and politically. Eventually this society would collapse, as the Last Man would himself destroy it out of boredom. History itself for Fukuyama then is a process that can never satisfy humanity, and his Hegelian-inspired theory of structural historical development at the end reveals itself to be another high-level cyclical interpretation of history as eternal conflict. Fukuyama notes at the beginning of the memoir that “I have been asked several times a week over the past three decades whether I wished to recant my argument.” In sum, no, Fukuyama sticks to his guns, but clarifies that his suggestion was more “that History, rather than ending, had simply paused on its way to an uncertain future.” So what is life like in the realm of the Last Man? As a memoir, it is less the story of a life than a narrative of intellectual development. The incidents and chapters have no discernible order; Fukuyama simply plucks things from his mind and memories at random to stage out. It makes for oddly compelling reading, mixing anecdotes with study guide-esque writeups of various intellectuals and books. Fukuyama's life is full of improbable connections and moments, with his family background ensconced in elite academic and political circles. His maternal grandfather was Shiro Kawata, an academic agricultural economist who was part of Japan's modernization drive. Kawata studied in imperial Germany before WWI, where he was somehow able to gain access to parts of the personal library of the economic historian and theorist Werner Sombart. Sombart, alongside Max Weber, was one of the great intellectuals of late imperial Germany, before supporting the Nazis in the 1930s. Sombart's work influenced generations of German-speaking academics, which was then translated and widely disseminated in English among American academics, and thereby influencing Anglosphere scholarship as a whole. Sombart is widely credited as having developed the term and theory of “late capitalism.” Fukuyama notes that from his grandfather's portion of Sombart's library, he inherited a first-edition copy of .

item.title: Octopus Chases a Laser Light
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: The ROV (remotely operated vehicle) Hercules was down 323 meters (1059 feet) in the Papahānaumokuākea National Marine Sanctuary west of Hawaii, looking around for researchers aboard the EV Nautilus. A small octopus was just doing octopus things when the ROV's measurement lights became clear on the ocean floor. What did the octopus do? It chased the lights, just like a cat would chase a laser toy, much to the delight of the scientists watching it. That's only the first two minutes of this video. There are other clips of small octopi looking for hidey holes and changing their colors. And as usual, the most delightful part of Nautilus' videos are the remarks from the researchers, who do this all the time and still find wonder in watching deep sea creatures in a their natural habitat. (via Metafilter)

item.title: Josh Goes Back to the Big Senate Data Dive to Obsess About Polling Error
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: Back in August I did a write-up on a deep dive on polling error put together by Republican consultant/pollster Pat Ruffini. When it comes to Ruffini’s work, I have a funny mix of assumptions and impulses. Ruffini’s a data guy and not a bullshitter. His numbers and analyses are real and solid. He’s also a Republican partisan. So he’s not above looking for the most favorable possibilities in the numbers. And I think it’s fair to say the series he’s done on this is generally aimed at Republicans and trying to send the message, “It might be okay” or “It’s not as bad as it looks.” At the same time, am eager for it to be as bad for Republicans or worse than it looks.Take that for what you will. Just a little truth in advertising and transparency for all involved. Ruffini just did a follow-up on this deep dive where, amazingly, there’s a new reason to think it might not be as bad for Republicans as it looks! Again, though, Ruffini’s a smart guy with a lot of data up his sleeves and he might be right.

item.author: Josh Marshall

item.title: The Sweet Enoughs
item.author: Flow State
item.content:encoded: Today we’re listening to The Sweet Enoughs, an Australian trio led by bassist Paul Bender. He started the group in the late 2010s along with his Hiatus Kaiyote bandmate Simon Mavin (keys) and Lachlan Mitchell (guitar). The group’s first record was 2020’s , a sort of easy listening / exotica themed record that we’ve excerpted on many mixes. Their new record, Another Helping of the Sweet Enoughs, plays a similar style, channeling mid-century composers like Les Baxter and Piero Umiliani. The record was executive produced by the fictional Greek yacht-faring maestro Yannis Dreamlake, who gives an exclusive interview that accompanies the album’s Bandcamp release.

item.title: LaTeX renderer
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: Inspired by Paul Ford and Aboard Foundary's new web app Tiny Little Office, which provides a suite of web app content editors (a Word Processor, Outliner, Presentation Builder, Spreadsheet, Calculator, Drawing Tool, Diagram Maker, Animator, Calendar, and Trip Planner).Tiny Little Office's signature trick is to store all of the document data in the section of the URL, so every document created using it becomes a bookmarkable and shareable link.Tiny Little Office inspired me to have Claude Code (Opus 5.5 Extra) build a similar tool that works with LaTeX. Here's the sequence of prompts I used:I want a tool where you can link to it with a fragment hash #code-here and it treats that code as LaTeX and renders it really effectively. It should also support a prefix which means the latex is compressed with a custom compression dictionary optimized for latex. Use the best available latex render library from a CDN (consider WebAssembly too). If loaded without a fragment hash show an editor you can paste latex into and then toggle to a "rendered" view. That rendered view should be bookmarkable. The #fragment view should let you switch to edit source too.Since it was working in my tools repo I told it to take inspiration from the mechanism used by my existing SVG in Markdown tool as protection against XSS risks:Safe from XSS? We could run in an iframe sandbox like we do on the SVG markdown render projectI had it copy the Gist/URL loading feature from that tool as well:We should have an option to load latex from a URL (or gist) similar to the markdown SVG tool

item.title: Forgotten Band: Mudhoney
item.author: Schill
item.content:encoded: There is something slightly ridiculous about calling Mudhoney a forgotten band.They were there when the Seattle music scene was turning into the biggest rock story on the planet. They released records on Sub Pop. They helped establish the sound that would eventually be labeled grunge. Kurt Cobain was a fan. Their music became part of the soundtrack to one of the most important alternative-rock movements of the late 1980s and early 1990s.And yet, when people talk about grunge today, Mudhoney often gets pushed several places down the list.Everybody remembers Nirvana.Everybody remembers Pearl Jam.Soundgarden and Alice in Chains get their share of attention.Then somebody mentions Mudhoney and you can practically see the question forming:“Wait… weren’t they one of those Seattle bands?”They were one of Seattle bands.Except they were there before almost everybody else.Before Grunge Was a ThingMudhoney formed in Seattle in 1988, emerging from the ashes of two hugely important underground bands: Green River and The Melvins-adjacent scene that was developing around the Pacific Northwest.The original lineup featured Mark Arm on vocals, Steve Turner on guitar, Matt Lukin on bass and Dan Peters on drums.If those names aren’t immediately familiar, the music should be.The guitars were distorted and fuzzy. The drums sounded like they were being played in a basement. Mark Arm’s vocals could shift from sarcastic sneering to full-on screaming without warning.And there was a willingness to sound completely out of control.That combination became one of the foundations of the Seattle sound.Mudhoney’s relationship with Sub Pop was crucial.The label was still a tiny operation when Mudhoney released their debut single, “Touch Me I’m Sick,” in 1988.That song became one of the defining recordings of the early Seattle scene.It was loud, nasty and catchy in exactly the right proportions.It also demonstrated something important about the bands coming out of Seattle.They weren’t trying to sound like polished arena-rock stars.They didn’t seem particularly interested in sounding fashionable either.Mudhoney sounded like a band that had spent too much time listening to punk and garage records and had decided to make everything louder.“Touch Me I’m Sick” became a cult classic, and Mudhoney quickly became one of the most recognizable names associated with Sub Pop.Suddenly Everybody Wanted to Be From SeattleBy the early 1990s, Seattle had become the center of the rock universe.Record companies were signing anything that had a flannel shirt and a distorted guitar.Bands that had spent years playing tiny clubs were suddenly being offered major-label contracts.Nirvana’s changed everything.Soundgarden broke through.Alice in Chains became a major rock act.The term “grunge” was suddenly everywhere.Mudhoney, however, never became a superstar.That wasn’t necessarily because they weren’t good enough.In fact, their refusal to chase mainstream success may have been part of the reason they remained so respected.They were never particularly interested in cleaning up their sound for radio.They didn’t suddenly start writing power ballads.They didn’t reinvent themselves to take advantage of the grunge explosion.They just kept being Mudhoney.The Problem With Being InfluentialMudhoney’s biggest historical problem is that they were more influential than commercially successful.That’s a strange position for a band to occupy.They helped create the sound.Other bands became famous for it.It’s similar to being the person who invents a recipe and then watching somebody else become famous after opening a restaurant serving it.Mudhoney helped establish the distorted, ugly, sarcastic side of Seattle rock.But when the rest of the world discovered Seattle, the spotlight landed elsewhere.They became the cool band’s favorite band.That’s great for credibility.It isn’t necessarily great for your Wikipedia page.They Had More Than One SongAnother reason Mudhoney gets overlooked is that casual listeners often know only “Touch Me I’m Sick.”That’s a shame because the band’s catalog is much deeper.Their self-titled 1989 album remains one of the essential documents of the early Sub Pop era.Then came Every Good Boy Deserves Fudge in 1991, arguably one of their strongest records.Instead of chasing the increasingly polished alternative-rock sound, Mudhoney doubled down on their weirdness.There were punk influences, garage-rock riffs, noisy experiments and surprisingly catchy melodies.They sounded like they didn’t care whether anybody understood what they were doing.That attitude was increasingly rare as alternative rock became a commercial industry.They Even Went Major LabelMudhoney eventually signed with Reprise Records and released in 1992.For a moment, it looked like the band might finally receive the commercial success that had eluded them.But the album demonstrated that Mudhoney could make the jump to a major label without completely losing their identity.They remained gloriously unconcerned with becoming the next Pearl Jam.Eventually they returned to the independent world and continued recording.And that’s one of the most impressive things about their story.They didn’t disappear when grunge faded.They didn’t become a nostalgia act.They just kept making records.The Band That Refused to Go AwayMudhoney’s longevity is actually one of the reasons they are so easy to overlook.They’re not a dramatic “what happened to them?” story.They never broke up for decades.They never had a spectacular fall from the top.That isn’t necessarily the kind of story that generates documentaries and endless nostalgia pieces.But it might be the better story.Mudhoney survived the grunge explosion, the death of grunge, the rise of alternative rock, the decline of alternative rock, the digital music revolution and the streaming era.They were still Mudhoney.Mark Arm’s Voice Remains Instantly RecognizableOne of the band’s greatest assets has always been Mark Arm.His voice doesn’t sound like a conventional rock singer.Sometimes it sounds like he’s barely holding the song together.That was perfect for Mudhoney.There is no mistaking him once you hear him.Steve Turner’s guitar work is equally important.Instead of the polished riffs that would dominate mainstream rock, Mudhoney embraced fuzz, feedback and noise.The guitars often sound like they’re being pushed beyond their limits.That’s part of the appeal.The imperfections become the sound.Mudhoney still has a loyal fan base.They still release music.They remain hugely respected by musicians and serious alternative-rock fans.But culturally, they have been overshadowed.The story of grunge has become a story about Nirvana, Pearl Jam, Soundgarden and Alice in Chains.Mudhoney is often treated as part of the opening chapter rather than one of the main characters.Because without bands like Mudhoney, the Seattle explosion would have looked very different.They helped create the environment that made the entire movement possible.They were there before the major labels came calling.They were there before the flannel shirts became a fashion statement.They were there before everybody suddenly claimed to have discovered Seattle.And they kept going after everybody else moved on.The Ultimate “Forgotten” BandMudhoney isn’t really forgotten.They’re something more interesting.Their influence is enormous compared with their mainstream profile.Their songs still sound filthy and energetic.Their early records remain essential listening for anyone interested in the origins of grunge.And their refusal to turn themselves into a polished commercial product is probably one reason their music has aged so well.If you only know Mudhoney because of “Touch Me I’m Sick,” you’ve barely scratched the surface.Play Every Good Boy Deserves Fudge.Then work your way through the later albums.You’ll find a band that wasn’t simply riding the grunge wave.They helped create the damn wave.And maybe that’s the weirdest part of Mudhoney’s legacy.They were never the biggest band in Seattle.They were never the richest.They were never the most famous.But when the history of alternative rock gets traced back far enough, their fingerprints are all over it.That’s not being forgotten.That’s being one of the bands everyone else forgot to thank.

item.title: Mr. Sardonicus
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: In the 1961 Willian Castle gothic horror film, physician Sir Robert Cargrave is summoned by his ex-girlfriend Maude to a spooky eastern European castle to treat her new husband, Baron Sardonicus. The Baron suffers from a face paralyzed into an evil grin that interferes with eating and speaking -a result of his grave robbing incident. He rules his roost with cruelty, and Dr. Cargrave is drawn into his plans to cure his malady with experimental procedures because he's afraid of what may happen to Maude. (Thanks, WTM!)

item.title: Is the MAGA Grift-Quickening Upon Us?
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: This is the weekly, free edition of The Backchannel. If you’d like to receive the free edition of The Backchannel in your inbox, you can subscribe here.Kimberly Guilfoyle, the recently defenestrated and soon-to-be-former Ambassador to Greece, has that stench about her of third-string corruption, the type that is hated by the righteous and sneered at by the corrupt. In Trumpworld setting up your own bribery-faucet meme coin and making billions is a baller move. Begging a MAGA-adjacent huckster to settle your Amex bill on the strength of once being Don Jr’s fiancée is sad. “Steal a little and they throw ya in jail / Steal a lot and they make you king …” But we seem quite suddenly to be seeing MAGA world become quite leaky. That’s not what we’re used to — what we’re used to is mammoth kinds of Trump and MAGA corruption more or less in plain sight. But now various MAGA capos are accusing each other, or dropping dimes on each other, as the reality of a possible Blue Wave or more comes into view.Another only-in-MAGA corruption story hit this afternoon. Or, I guess, alleged corruption story since it’s not altogether clear which player in the story is the crook or more of a crook.

item.title: The Muffled Thud of Fire in the Hole
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: One warm spring night in 2011, a young man named Travis Hughes stood on the back deck of the Alpha Tau Omega fraternity house at Marshall University, in West Virginia, and was struck by what seemed to him — under the influence of powerful inebriants, not least among them the clear ether of youth itself — to be an excellent idea: he would shove a bottle rocket up his ass and blast it into the sweet night air. And perhaps it was an excellent idea. What was not an excellent idea, however, was to misjudge the relative tightness of a 20-year-old sphincter and the propulsive reliability of a 20-cent bottle rocket. What followed ignition was not the bright report of a successful blastoff, but the muffled thud of fire in the hole.

This one used the default Claude iPhone app (chat mode, not Claude Code mode), where I prompted Claude Opus 5.5 Max with:Build a three js game called "Tree appreciator" - it shows you two algorithmically generated trees and the game mechanics is about appreciating the differences between them. item.title: Sally Rooney Stands By Her Principles
item.author: Kelsey McKinney
item.content:encoded: Sally Rooney, one of the most popular novelists alive, says she will no longer sell her books in the U.K. In 2025, the British government proscribed Palestine Action as a terrorist organization, and in August of that year, Rooney published an op-ed in titled, "I support Palestine Action. If this makes me a ‘supporter of terror’ under UK law, so be it." Now, because the laws have not changed, Rooney and her publisher Faber & Faber announced this week that they will no longer be publishing her work in the U.K.Rooney's novels have sold more than 2 million copies in the U.K. alone, a monumental number for any modern novelist. Her books and Conversations with Friends have been adapted for television. In her op-ed last year, Rooney stated that she intended to give the royalties from her books sold in the U.K., as well as her residuals from the television adaptions of her novels, to Palestine Action, a direct action network known for disrupting weapon manufacturers that sell arms to Israel. Under U.K. anti-terrorism laws, Rooney's publisher can no longer give her the royalties for her novels, knowing that she will donate them to Palestine Action, without putting them both at risk.Technically, Rooney's books could still be sold in the U.K., but she would not be paid for their sales. Her publisher did not want to withhold the earnings from her. "As such, and in full agreement with Sally, we have taken the decision that we can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format," Faber & Faber said in a statement.

item.title: Spain Reminds The USWNT Where They Stand
item.author: Abigail Segel
item.content:encoded: For decades, the U.S. Women's National Team stood at the top of the mountain, where the air is thinnest. They defended their position with ferocity. They didn't win every major tournament, but they won most of them, and were contenders in all. Their identity on the pitch, more than anything, was being the best.That changed with the 2023 World Cup, when the two-time defending champions flamed out in the round of 16 after barely surviving the group stage. Spain went on to win the tournament, deservedly so. That result, combined with Spaniard-heavy Barcelona's simultaneous surge on the European stage, made it clear that had pushed the USWNT off the side of the mountain and taken their place at the summit.The USWNT might have won the 2024 Olympics, but anyone with eyes that see will tell you that Spain remains the better team. The USWNT are under no illusions about this. "All of these things that we're teaching are for this opponent," head coach Emma Hayes told her players Saturday after losing to Spain, 2-0, in the first of two friendlies. "And the reason I say that is because that's our barometer of success."

item.title: Stutterer
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: Greenwood (played by Matthew Needham) is a lonely typographer who suffers from a serious stutter, and it makes his life hard. He's found ways around it to some extent, but everyday tasks are a constant reminder of his disability, like trying to get through to a customer service representative on the phone. His thoughts, however, are fluid and even poetic. The bright spot is that he's built a long distance text relationship with a woman named Ellie. Greenwood's anxiety blows up to eleven when she has an opportunity to travel to London and meet him in person. highlights the inner struggles of those who suffer from a condition most of us don't understand. The film won an Oscar in 2016 for Best Live Action Short Film, plus a slew of other awards, and is only now available for all of us to see. I highly recommend it. (via kottke)

item.title: Warhammer 40K Is Cool
item.author: Patrick Wyman
item.content:encoded: In the grim darkness of the far future, 40,000 years from now, an immortal corpse-Emperor sits atop his Golden Throne on Earth, watching over the trillions upon trillions of human beings scattered across the galaxy. For ten thousand years, the Emperor hasn’t spoken or moved from that Golden Throne, and those masses of humans are ruled by the Imperium of Man in the Emperor’s name. Their often short existences are spent within the Imperium’s authoritarian systems that value ignorance over knowledge and stasis over change. Human life is cheap, and the Imperium spends it freely on never-ending wars with a variety of aliens and the forces of Chaos, which inhabit an alternate dimension known as the Warp.Earth—Terra—is a hellscape, a city-planet packed with so many people that an accurate count is impossible, its oceans long since boiled away and its original surface buried beneath millennia of haphazard construction. The Imperium is a creaking, ramshackle realm where cruelty, hierarchy, and suppression are facts of life. Its greatest warriors, the Space Marines, are genetically altered monstrosities, created through processes that kill more than they successfully manufacture. Technology is controlled by closed-minded zealots who fear nothing more than innovation. Of course, the Imperium has an Inquisition, which roots out heresy of all kinds, and an official church (the Ecclesiarchy) dedicated to unquestioning worship of the Emperor.The aliens—xenos, in the parlance of the universe—are no better. The Orks live only for fighting; the elf-like Aeldari care little for lesser beings; their dark elf Drukhari cousins subsist on torture and pain; the Necrons are living-metal horrors who traded mortal life for soulless immortality tens of millions of years ago; the insectoid Tyranids, controlled by a hivemind, exist solely to consume every bit of biomass in their path; and even the T’au, the newest addition to the galaxy, who value the Greater Good above all, aren’t to be trusted.

item.title: AI is mass decompiling games. That's both awesome and scary.
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: Indie game developer Popcar talks about the recent wave of AI-powered decompilation of existing games, enabling weird mashups between existing games, and producing a boom in game preservation projects to get old games working on new hardware (often in a browser using WebAssembly).I like how this piece captures both the positives and the negatives of this new development:Most people already realized the scary part by now. If AI can decompile games and software, then the entire tech industry is about to explode. Anybody can decompile other software and use it any way they'd like, and nobody can stop them. Companies can steal from competitors. Your paid game or app can be open-sourced against your will. This isn't exclusive to old video games, we can apply this to software. [...]This is also a big win for preservation. Old games can be ported, modified, enhanced, and made much more easily accessible than before. [...[With console makers going all in on digital and games becoming entirely unplayable due to servers shutting down, this is news. We could own software we bought regardless of what the company thinks.

item.title: Manchester United Is Eating Itself Alive
item.author: Luis Paez-Pumar
item.content:encoded: In terms of things you simply do not want to see happening at the club you support within the first two months of the season, one of your star players blasting the entire organizational hierarchy has to be pretty high up there. That's exactly what's happening at Manchester United, following a brutal start (one win, three draws, two losses, and 13th place) to what was supposed to be an exemplary Premier League season and a listless and frustrating 2-0 defeat Tuesday to Atlético Madrid in the second match day of the Champions League campaign. The locker room is now officially unsettled, as Lisandro Martínez made clear in his postgame interview. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LE3Ux23BNLo That's Martínez, perhaps still in his feelings about a confrontation at the end of the match with his Argentine compatriots on Atleti, blasting United from top to bottom. Of particular note are his quotes directed at technical director Jason Wilcox, whom the center back feels did not do enough to allow United to build on last season's successes: "We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well." item.title: ALERT: Trump DOJ Begins Active Election Interference in California
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: What Election Officials Have Long FearedIn a major escalation of its multi-prong attempts to interfere in the midterm elections, the Trump DOJ has given California 48 hours to take steps to prevent an unknown number of alleged noncitizen voters in Los Angeles County from voting — or face legal action, Reuters exclusively reports.This new Trump DOJ initiative is different from its earlier, largely unsuccessful efforts to obtain voter information from various states. Instead, it is now demanding that Los Angeles County take affirmative steps to prevent the counting of ballots cast by people on a list provided by DOJ who it alleges are “likely noncitizen voters” who received mail-in ballots.The Trump DOJ’s demands came in the form of a threat letter Tuesday to California Secretary ‌of State Shirley Weber from acting Deputy Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter — an extraordinary intervention by the department’s No. 2 official.The existence of the letter was confirmed by the Justice Department. It’s not clear how DOJ came up with its list, which was provided to Los Angeles County on a “password-protected thumb drive.” Past attempts by the Trump administration to identify noncitizens who are allegedly registered to vote have been deeply flawed and wildly inaccurate.In the letter, McCotter sets an arbitrary 48-hour deadline for California to review the DOJ list, but the more alarming development is what other steps McCotter demands that California take, according to Reuters: to send ballots to people who appear on the DOJ list until their citizenship status has been confirmed; the mail-in ballots already returned by people who appear on the DOJ list; the mail-in ballots of those on the DOJ list until their citizenship status has been confirmed.These are the most aggressive steps the Trump administration has taken in its jihad against mythical noncitizen voting, which it greatly exaggerates as a pretext for the federal takeover of elections, the delegitimization of free and fair elections, and the disregard of election results that it disfavors.“Allowing noncitizens to vote cancels citizen votes,” McCotter wrote in the letter, echoing one element of the Trump administration’s long-running disinformation campaign. McCotter threatened to seek emergency relief in court if California does not comply with his demands.The latest move — challenging entire batches of ballots and threatening to go to court unless Los Angeles County undertakes specific steps in its handling of the election — comes as the election in California is already underway. Mail-in ballots were sent out to every voter in the state beginning on Oct. 5, the same day that ballot drop-off centers opened statewide.This is the kind of Trump administration interference that election officials nationwide have been dreading and planning for this entire election cycle. The executive branch has no constitutional role in the conduct of federal elections, which is delegated to the states.It’s not yet clear if the Trump DOJ sent similar demand letters to election officials in other states.Essayli Likely to be Booted As LA USAIn another blow to President Trump’s U.S. attorneys scheme in blue states, a federal judge appears poised to disqualify Bill Essayli as the top federal prosecutor in Los Angeles, Bloomberg reports.Essayli was already disqualified by the court from serving as acting U.S. attorney, but the Trump DOJ tried to sidestep that ruling by making Essayli the first assistant U.S. attorney — with all the powers to run the office.But the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, in a similar case in Nevada, ruled that first assistants assume the power of the U.S. attorney only if they were already installed when the office was vacated.Not Just DHS — DOJ Targets Rep. Omar, TooD.C. U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro is stumbling all over herself to get in on the targeting of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN) by the Trump administration.The day after DHS’ Homeland Security Investigations executed a search warrant on Omar’s D.C. home in a what appears to be a bogus investigation into how her late father obtained naturalized U.S. citizenship, Pirro went on Fox News to declare that Omar is under separate DOJ investigation over her financial disclosure forms.The public announcement of a criminal investigation by Pirro would be highly irregular at any time, but especially coming just three weeks before the election, further cementing the politicized nature of the Trump administration’s targeting of Omar … as if there was any doubt.In the immigration investigation, family members of Omar have been issued grand jury subpoenas, the NYT reports.DOJ Stiffed Minnesota Over ICE ShootingsYou can be forgiven for thinking that the Trump DOJ had relented after six months and began sharing evidence with Minnesota in the three ICE shootings during Operation Metro Surge. Hennepin County prosecutor Mary Moriarty held a press conference in July announcing the evidence-sharing agreement that had been reached with DOJ.But in new court filings yesterday, Minnesota officials, including Moriarty, revealed that the Trump DOJ ceased cooperating again after her press conference. And the impression they leave is that the agreement, which was struck with the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Minneapolis and led to an initial round of evidence sharing, was quickly scotched by Main Justice after news of it broke.In her declaration, Moriarty says that she spoke with U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen on Sept. 10, “who told me, in sum and substance, that evidence sharing from the USAO as agreed to in the June 26 letter would be on pause indefinitely ‘in light of challenges with D.C.’”The new revelations come in a federal lawsuit that Minnesota filed in D.C. seeking to obtain evidence gathered by DHS and DOJ in the shootings of Renee Good, Alex Pretti, and Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis. Minnesota has already charged ICE agent Christian Castro in the Sosa-Celis shooting.Texas Considers Charges Against ICE AgentIn Houston, the district attorney is considering charging an ICE agent who allegedly ran his vehicle over a Mexican national Saturday with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. ICE’s claim that the man ran in front of the ICE agent’s vehicle is undermined by security camera footage showing the car veering toward the fleeing man. One of his legs was broken, not both, as previously reported.After firing the publisher and editor of Stars and Stripes, the Pentagon has installed one of its own public affairs officials to run the once-independent military newspaper — and he will keep his Pentagon job while doing it, Military.com reports.In “The Dawn Of The Self-Funding Pentagon,” Spencer Ackerman warns of the dangers of the “deal” that the Trump administration has stuck to give the Pentagon an equity position in Venezuela’s oil fields outside of the congressional appropriations process: “This is a step in the direction of the U.S. military holding a revenue-generating stake in sectors of another country’s civilian economy.”AI Did Me In: The Kim Guilfoyle StoryAll the credit to the WSJ for the devastating series of stories that led to the forced resignation of Kimberly Guilfoyle as U.S. ambassador to Greece. In surveying the aftermath of its work, the newspaper had a few more gems to drop about Guilfoyle’s final days: (the lyrics from the Lake Street Dive song are unbelievably on point): Guilfoyle decorated the official ambassadorial residence with large self-portraits.: After the second major WSJ story, which relied on text messages showing her soliciting a major GOP donor to pay off her $100,000 Amex bill, Guilfoyle told White House officials that the text messages were AI-generated. “The officials didn’t believe her claims,” according to the WSJ.Did she find out at the same time we did? This account raises the possibility that Guilfoyle found out that she was being asked to resign when it was announced by the White House, although that is not the only plausible interpretation:During a Tuesday-morning prep session for his new press secretary Katie Zacharia’s first briefing at the White House, the president instructed Zacharia to tell the world that he was asking Guilfoyle to resign, people familiar with the matter said. Trump didn’t speak directly to Guilfoyle before making the decision, one of the people said.

item.title: Punch Bowl Now More Turd Than Punch
item.author: Giri Nathan
item.content:encoded: How quickly can the owner of a reigning championship team spend down a sudden windfall of goodwill? James Dolan has spent the NBA offseason exploring that hypothetical, and he appears to be a gifted speedrunner.The owner of the New York Knicks began his work before the job was even done this past June, inviting Donald Trump to Game 3 of the NBA Finals. That wound up being the team's only loss in an otherwise torrid 15-game playoff stretch. Then, at the team's victory parade, mere days after he'd funded the first title in 53 years for a team beloved by America's biggest city, Dolan took the mic and glowered. To cap off an event that united an estimated 2 million fans in communal joy, the team owner used his time in the pulpit to (predictably) take a shot at Mayor Zohran Mamdani and (inexplicably) question the Knicks fandom of parade attendees. "I don't need your vote," he told the fans, for some reason.For all the justified criticisms of Dolan over the years, he has typically been willing to spend his money on the team. A fan could have reasonably expected that an owner who has already spent big on some catastrophic Knicks rosters would happily spend big to return a lucrative, championship-winning roster, even under the current collective bargaining agreement, which punishes high spenders. But this was not the case. Just four days after the Knicks lifted the trophy, Dolan told WFAN that he would not spend into the second apron to keep the team intact. "We're willing to stretch, but there's certain things in the NBA that you'd have to be suicidal to do," he said. "One of them is the second apron."

item.title: Good Baseball Isn’t Necessarily Beautiful
item.author: Ray Ratto
item.content:encoded: The American League Championship Series is every bit an American League production, which is to say that it is not for the dilettante, or anything close to an easy watch. It is for people who choose to view sports in their leisure time as penance for past misdeeds rather than as a reward for past service. You don't sit back and enjoy it passively; you may not enjoy it at all. Instead you lean in with clenched fists and teeth in full-lock grind, because this is the business that you and they have chosen, and the aesthetic you and they have embraced. One of these teams is going to play in the World Series, and far more concerning for you lightweights, it could still be the Cleveland Guardians.The AL, you see, is not the Tampa Bay Rays, the perennially competitive team defined by pluck, platooning, and small contracts. Their calling card is more than those low payrolls and zeal for doing the things everyone else dismisses as Little League nonsense. They have been the fourth-best team in the sport over the last two decades, and this may well be their most complete team yet. They win because of their seemingly indomitable pitching, a roster full of opportunistic multi-tool players whose talents mesh delightfully and whose shortcomings somehow do not clump up in unsightly blobs, and perhaps also due to the cool multi-colored Devil Rays jerseys they wear sometimes, which recall their franchise origins, and specifically to the part when religious groups claimed they were honoring Satanic influences and were taken seriously enough that the franchise dropped the Devil for good.They are the best team in the AL, but they are their own thing. The AL this year is actually much closer to Cleveland, a sometimes-hard-to-watch surprise team that really isn't that surprising. They won 13 fewer regular-season games in winning their benighted division but, like Tampa, Cleveland got a first-round bye and all the advantages that come with it. They are in the ALCS after having earned it—inelegantly, perhaps, and in uniforms that hearken back to a time when the only colors in the world were navy blue and red and fonts were something only runty graphic designers understood. But they earned it all the same.

item.title: Whoa, the Lion Nebula!
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: Massive stars undergo supernova explosions at the end of their lives, but these kinds of events are few and far in between. Most of the universe’s stars have lower masses, like the one belonging to NGC 2392. When a lower-mass star can no longer sustain itself with nuclear reactions in its core, the star becomes unstable and pulsates, losing its mass by shedding its outer layers, which then turn into shells of gas and dust called a planetary nebula. (Stars at this life stage are responsible for producing much of the universe’s observable dust.) The star’s radiation drives the ejected material away, leaving behind the very hot stellar core, also known as a white dwarf.In the Lion Nebula’s case, the death of the oxygen-rich central star has left behind a white dwarf that is “cooking” everything from the inside and producing a bubble of ionized gas as it does. The gas bubble, which forms the lion’s face, is expanding over time and destroying dust that is in its path. Understanding why the swept-up gas has a complex structure of rings and shells, a common feature in planetary nebulae, is an ongoing endeavor.The mane of the lion is the interior of a dust shell that is being illuminated by the white dwarf at the center. The tufts of hair, which look like cometary tails of material, are compact clumps of dust that have survived the stellar core’s radiation and protect the material that lies behind them.Webb’s imagery “freezes” this planetary nebula in time, though the star’s death, and its tumultuous effects, go on. NGC 2392 will continue to undergo changes as its gas and dust migrate away from the stellar core. Astronomers estimate the lion will eventually disperse in approximately 10,000 years — a relatively short period in astronomical terms.The Hubble imaged the nebula in 2000 in visible light, but the JWST’s infrared cameras are higher resolution and better at capturing the gas and dust details.

item.title: Holy shit, Katie Zacharia is super fucking bad at her job

item.content:encoded: I know that I’m breaking no new ground when I point out that every member of the Donnyverse is a low-wattage shit-wit, blessed with absolutely zero qualifications for the jobs to which they’ve been assigned.You’ve got a gin-soaked, failed weekend chat-show host running the military. A lady who arranged rigged wrestling matches is now in charge of education. A reality-show never-was has been tasked with making sure planes don’t fall from the sky. It was like watching a clip of a robot fail. Quick, someone reboot Katie!“He had a historic one-day war, and now we are— have a— booming economy, and a— a great relationship [another interminably long pause] Oh shit, can somebody reboot Katie again?I really need to caution you that if you try to watch the whole thing, you may end up stupider than when you started. What a crap-show. Katie was stiff. Uncomfortable. Non-human. Unwilling or unable to make eye contact. She took only three questions from the press, and then mercifully booked it out of there after fourteen minutes. “Some White House officials are already wondering how long she’ll keep the job. They tell CNN’s Kaitlan Collins her performance was unlikely to satisfy President Trump. One White House official called the appearance, quote, ‘unusual.’ Another called it ‘brutal.’”The question everyone’s now asking is, ‘can she Anthony Scaramucci?’ Tony Scaramucci, you’ll recall, is the weirdo who famously lasted only eleven days as one of Preznit Fuckwit’s press secretaries. The Mooch got shitcanned for saying goofy shit like, ‘I’m not Steve Bannon, I’m not trying to suck my own cock.’Thanks for sharing, Mooch. You know, I could have gone my entire life without knowing that about Rotting Stevie Three-Shirts.Meanwhile, you’ll be shocked to learn that Katie Zacharia may or may not be lying about her resumé. She claims to be a lawyer, but when the press pressed her for details (Ha ha! See what I did there?),Katie’s answer was a non-answer.Reporter: “you said Zacharia is an attorney. Where did she pass the bar exam? What state?”Zacharia: Yeah, no. China isn’t a state.One cannot take an American state bar exam in China. Bar exams are administered at designated testing locations in each state of the union. Are Katie Zacharia and trump lying when they say she is an attorney? If not, then she needs to disclose in what state she passed the bar.Look, Katie Zacharia ticks all the Donnyverse boxes. She’s a liar, she’s evasive, she’s a fucking weirdo, she’s unqualified, and she’s absolute shit at her job. If that’s not a deal-breaker for any of the men who do Dear Leader’s bidding, then it shouldn’t be for Katie.Our piss-drunk Secretary of Death hasn’t lost his job, after butt-dialing classified war plans to a reporter, or depleting our nation’s supply of missiles, or destroying military readiness, or blundering us into an unwinnable war, or any of the other fucked-up shit he’s pulled. Bobby Brainworms still has his job, after single-handedly creating a measles epidemic. Liddle Marco Big-Shoes still has his job, even after It’s only the women who have been pushed out of their jobs during our Misogynist-in-Chief’s second reign. Pam Bondi. Tulsi Gabbard. Kristi Noem. And, most recently, Kimberly Gargoyle. Maybe it’s Dear Leader who should be better at job. Maybe he should stop hiring men just because they look like they came ‘straight out of central casting.’Maybe Donny should stop hiring woman simply because they remind him of the daughter he wants to quote-unquote ‘date,’ if that’s what we’re charitably going to call it.Come on — let Katie Zacharia keep her job. She’s so bad, she’s good. She’s entertaining as fuck — and at least when she screws up, it won’t result in planes colliding in mid air, or the proliferation of human shit geysers.Look at this idiot, on the tarmac in Alaska last night. He had — to walk in a straight line, into the wide-open door of his waiting helicopter.Spoiler alert: , inexplicably meandering towards the rear of the copter. Wither doest thou wander, dipshit?It’s only at the last second that he apparently snaps out of his reverie and remembers why doors exist. Holy shit. Donny’s brain has gone fuckity-bye.But please — tell me once again how Joe Biden was too old and icky and smelly and decrepit to properly to his job. That’s such a cool story.Hey — it’s Daily Claudia time.here’s Ms. Spouse in the back yard on May 27, 2013.and here she is at a restaurant on Lake Mahopac that has gone through many names over the years, but it was called Blu when we were there on April 27, 2018.Have a great Wednesday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Leadership Dispatch: Question your questions
item.author: bounces+n4u44reogwfvhxdewq2t6h66329mwslhe4wp@ckespa.joshdoody.com
item.content:encoded: This week's Leadership Dispatch is about when to ask questions and what sort of questions to ask. It can be almost automatic to ask questions in certain situation, but sometimes those questions cause more harm than good.This week, I'm sharing a simple framework for when to ask questions and what kind of questions to ask when trying to keep your team on track.Before you ask questions of your team, consider you’re asking those questions. You’ll often be asking for one of these two reasons: questions are designed to gather information. “Why do we think this customer issue seems to be coming up a lot lately?” questions are designed to elicit an answer from a predefined set of acceptable responses. “Which of these two features do we want to prioritize first?”Be careful when you ask Discovery-type questions at the wrong time.You’re in a tightly scheduled meeting with a specific end time, which is essentially . The meeting is wrapping up as people gather their things and push back their chairs, when the leader says, “Okay, we’re pretty much done here. Anyone have anything else they want to talk about?”You can probably the collective groan from everyone else in that room.Because the leader asked an open-ended Discovery-type question when they didn’t actually want to discover anything. Suddenly, anyone in the room has the power to keep everyone there indefinitely rather than getting the team out of there and back to work.Instead, they could ask a Direction-type question like “Our next meeting is on Monday at 10:00 AM, right?” or just not ask any questions at all.A tell that you should not ask a question is that you are either hoping no one will answer, or hoping for a very specific answer while dreading other answers. In this case, the leader is for silence or “Nope!” while dreading other answers like “Actually, this is slightly off topic but it’s something that I’ve been thinking about for a while…”When you ask questions, there’s a very good chance will feel obligated to answer. Are you you want to hear that answer?
